title: Stewardship gates, RFC acceptance criteria, and deprecation workflow for design primitives
creator: Aisha R. Kaur
description: Introduce a concise, enforceable set of stewardship gates and an RFC acceptance checklist for contributions to the Design System (tokens, buttons, tables, charts). Define a formal deprecation workflow that balances developer migration cost, telemetry, and visual parity guarantees. This ticket codifies reviewer roles, risk tiers, automated checks, and communication cadences so teams can land changes with predictable impact.
acceptance_criteria: A documented RFC checklist that design owners and reviewers use to accept/close RFCs
A three-tier risk classification (low / medium / high) and mapped reviewer requirements for each tier
A deprecation playbook with timelines, migration guidance, and telemetry signals to trigger accelerated rollback or quarantine
Automated lint rules and preview artifacts created for every PR touching tokens or core components
A published Confluence page and a pinned Console dashboard link for ongoing deprecations and active RFCs
proposed_changes: Gate 0 (Intake): submit RFC template + Figma token snapshot + examples of consumer usage
Gate 1 (Design Review): UX impact, accessibility checklist, visual tests for tokens and components
Gate 2 (Engineering Review): performance/DOM/slotting checks for buttons/tables + bundling/treeshake notes
Gate 3 (Compatibility): migration guide, codemods or wrappers, and telemetry events to track usage of deprecated APIs
Deprecation policy: soft-deprecate (6 weeks notice) then hard-deprecate after metric-driven review; emergency rollback path for regressions

decisions: Adopt three-tier risk model: low (visual-only tokens), medium (layout & spacing tokens, minor API), high (structural components or token renames affecting platform).
Require at least one cross-team review for medium/high risk RFCs (design + eng + platform owner).
All token renames must include a codemod or automated mapping for repositories contributing >1% of daily render volume.
Deprecations will publish a migration guide and a timeline; metrics will be checked at week 3 and week 6 to determine whether to extend or accelerate removal.
